terrain.label: Terrain
terrain.detail: Adaptive hypsometric tint. Deep-sea blue → shallow cyan → lowland green → highland brown → snow white. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers. On by default.

landsea.label: Land/Sea
landsea.detail: Binary blue/green shading to quickly distinguish ocean from land. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers.

plates.label: Plates
plates.detail: Each tectonic plate is colored distinctly. Plates are generated by the Cortial (2019) spherical Voronoi partition — Poisson-disc seeds + synchronized BFS. Colors cycle from a 15-color palette. Can stack over any base/thematic layer.

boundaries.label: Crust & Boundaries
boundaries.detail: Plate interiors colored by crust type: continental = warm brown, oceanic = grey-blue, transitional = olive. Hotspot chains = magenta. Ancient orogenies = dark gold. Rifts = cyan. Boundaries by type: convergent = red (subduction/collision), divergent = green (ridges/rifts), transform = yellow (strike-slip). Feature lines always on top.

ucc.label: UCC Classification
ucc.detail: Unified Climate Classification (UCC) profile v1 main-class colouring: the supply–demand grade picks the hue family (arid = warm red-orange / semi-arid = pale warm / transitional = olive-gold / humid = green — the Köppen reading habit where dry is warm-coloured), and the thermal band (polar/cold/temperate/tropical) shifts value within the family (colder = greyer); ocean cells use deep blues with the thermal band only (no supply axis). Classes are computed at export time with frozen, globally shared thresholds — the frontend never re-classifies. Modifiers (strong seasonality / seasonal water stress) appear in the cell panel's climate descriptors group. The layer is empty on exports that predate the classification fields. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers (single thematic slot, radio).

koppen.label: Köppen Climate
koppen.desc: Köppen–Geiger on land, with a marine temperature extension
koppen.detail: Land uses the Köppen–Geiger colors. The ocean is tropical where the coldest monthly temperature exceeds 18 °C and non-tropical elsewhere. Dark blue marks ocean without classification data. These bands do not indicate sea ice.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.desc: Annual mean temperature (blue=cold → white=0°C → red=hot; monthly mode varies by month)
temperature.detail: On land and at sea, annual and monthly temperatures use the same −40 to +40 °C scale. Blue is cold, white is 0 °C, and red is warm. Areas without data are transparent.

precipitation.label: Precipitation
precipitation.desc: Annual precipitation (yellow=dry → green → blue=wet, log; monthly mode varies by month)
precipitation.detail: The logarithmic scale shows precipitation over land and sea, from pale yellow in dry areas to dark blue in wet areas. Annual totals and monthly totals use separate ranges. Areas without data are transparent.

temperatureError.label: Temperature Error ΔT
temperatureError.desc: Model − NCEP per-grid observation (blue=model too cold · red=too warm)
temperatureError.detail: Per-cell annual temperature minus the NCEP/NCAR per-grid observed climatology: ΔT = model T − observed T(lat,lon). The observation carries real orography (a plateau ≈ −5 °C, not the +18 °C zonal mean), so the deviation reflects model error rather than elevation. Diverging scale, fixed ±20°C range: blue=model too cold, white=0, red=model too warm. Earth-only diagnostic (a fictional world has no observed reference); land-only. Mutually exclusive (radio).

precipitationError.label: Precipitation Error ΔP
precipitationError.desc: Model − GPCP per-grid observation (blue=model too dry · red=too wet)
precipitationError.detail: Per-cell annual precipitation minus the GPCP v2.3 per-grid observation: ΔP = model P − observed P(lat,lon). The observation carries real land/ocean contrast, so the deviation reflects model error rather than the 'zonal mean includes ocean rain' artifact. Diverging scale, fixed ±2000mm range: blue=model too dry, white=0, red=model too wet. Earth-only diagnostic; land-only. Mutually exclusive (radio).

pressureError.label: ΔSLP Deviation
pressureError.desc: Model monthly ΔP − NCEP per-grid ΔSLP (blue=model too weak · red=too strong)
pressureError.detail: Monthly pressure anomaly minus the NCEP per-grid ΔSLP (canonical definition: SLP − same-month ocean band mean, M2-A0③). Diverging scale, fixed ±20 hPa range. Monthly-only (the annual stationary contrast lives in the Pressure Anomaly layer); selecting it auto-enables monthly mode. Earth-only diagnostic (a fictional world has no observed reference). High ice-cap cells are greyed out (the reanalysis SLP is a hypothetical reduction there — no trustworthy reference). Colored over both land and ocean. Mutually exclusive (radio).

windError.label: Wind Error
windError.desc: Model − NCEP per-grid vector wind deviation arrows (blue=weak · red=strong)
windError.detail: Annual vector wind deviation (Δu, Δv) = (model u − observed u, model v − observed v). Arrows show the deviation vector — direction = deviation direction, length ∝ magnitude, colour = magnitude (blue=weak → red=strong, fixed 0…10 m/s range). Earth-only diagnostic; coloured over both land and ocean. Overlay — stack alongside the wind field.

currentError.label: Current Error
currentError.desc: Model − SODA per-grid vector current deviation arrows (blue=weak · red=strong)
currentError.detail: Annual vector current deviation (Δu, Δv) = (model u − observed u, model v − observed v). Arrows show the deviation vector — direction = deviation direction, length ∝ magnitude, colour = magnitude (blue=weak → red=strong, fixed 0…0.2 m/s range). Earth-only diagnostic; ocean-only. Overlay — stack alongside the current field.

pressure.label: Pressure Anomaly
pressure.detail: Annual mode shows the annual-mean pressure anomaly (12-month mean of the canonical ΔP: SLP − same-month ocean band mean, ±20 hPa symmetric scale) — the stationary land–sea contrast: winter/summer high-pressure asymmetry, subtropical oceanic highs, sub-/anti-star heating contrast; works for engine-built worlds and Earth alike. Monthly mode shows the monthly ΔP (same canonical definition) on a diverging scale. Blue=low pressure (thermal lows / monsoon troughs) · red=high pressure (cold highs / subtropical highs). Colored over both land and ocean. Mutually exclusive (radio).

slp.label: Sea-level Pressure
slp.desc: Absolute SLP (raw NCEP field, blue=low · red=high)
slp.detail: Obs-root only: the raw NCEP slp.mon.ltm absolute sea-level pressure field read directly — no band reference, no anomaly convention, no banding/cliff artefacts. Diverging ±40 hPa centred on 1013.25. High ice-cap cells are greyed out (the reanalysis SLP is a hypothetical reduction there — not data to consume). Annual mode shows slp_annual; monthly mode shows the monthly SLP. Mutually exclusive (radio).

biomes.label: Whittaker Biomes
biomes.detail: Whittaker (1975) temperature-precipitation two-axis classification. Tropical rainforest=deep green·savanna=pale yellow-green·desert=beige·temperate forest=mid green·grassland=gold·boreal=blue-grey·tundra=grey-brown·ice=white·ocean=deep blue·lake=light blue. Mutually exclusive with Köppen (one of four).

npp.label: Net Primary Productivity
npp.desc: NPP heatmap (Miami model, warm beige→deep green)
npp.detail: Net primary productivity from the Miami model (Lieth 1975). Warm beige=low (desert <200) → deep green=high (rainforest >2000). Normalized to 0–3000 gC/m²/yr.

domesticable.label: Domestication Potential
domesticable.detail: Domestication potential via Whittaker biome lookup (Diamond 1997 framework). Gold=high herbivores+high crops·orange=high herbivores only·light green=high crops only·transparent=low. Temperate grassland is all-high.

soil.label: Soil Type
soil.detail: USDA soil orders derived from parent rock + climate (temperature/precipitation). Mollisol=deep green (temperate grassland, fertile)·Alfisol=olive·Oxisol/Ultisol=red (tropical/subtropical weathering, poor)·Aridisol=yellow·Spodosol/Gelisol=grey·Inceptisol/Entisol=light grey (young soils). Fertility feeds agricultural potential.

provinces.label: Biogeographic Provinces
provinces.detail: Two-level division by continental connectivity (realm) + contiguous biome (province). Colors cycle from the plate palette; same color = same province. References Wallace/Udvardy regionalization.

habitable.label: Habitability Grade
habitable.detail: Habitability grade = a 0–100 product of an asymmetric human-climate-niche band (peak 13 °C, Xu 2020) and an aridity ramp. Coastal access is an orthogonal dimension (distance_to_coast_km), not part of the score. Dark = polar/arid · brown = marginal · amber = moderate · green = good · teal = excellent temperate-humid. No hard zero — cool-wet oceanic ET (Faroese-type) sits mid-range: liveable but not farmable. Mutually exclusive (radio).

agriculture.label: Agriculture Grade
agriculture.detail: Agriculture grade = a hard zero below the Köppen C/D tree-line (warmest month >10°C), then a product of growing-degree-day (base 10°C, McMaster 1997), water, and soil-fertility factors. Grey = no crops · beige = marginal · yellow = moderate · gold = excellent farmland. Independent of habitability. Mutually exclusive (radio).

currents.label: Ocean Currents
currents.desc: Surface currents (arrows or particle flow; magenta=warm·cyan=cold)
currents.detail: Surface flow field from the Stommel wind-driven circulation model. Arrows: direction=flow, length∝speed, magenta=warm·cyan=cold, sampled on a ~8° grid and crisp at any zoom. Switch on Particle flow at the top of the layer panel to advect particles along the field; trail length reflects speed. Currents use the annual-mean field (monthly currents are not yet in the data contract). Freely stackable.

winds.label: Winds
winds.desc: Surface winds (arrows colored by temperature, particles colored by speed; monthly mode shows that month's wind)
winds.detail: Near-surface wind field from three-cell circulation + geostrophic wind. Arrows: direction=wind, length∝speed, color=temperature (blue=−20°C→green=0°C→red=+35°C), showing heat transport / cold-air paths. Switch on Particle flow at the top of the layer panel to advect particles along the field; color becomes speed (blue=slow→green→yellow→red=fast) and the field follows the selected month in monthly mode (the Earth reference only has annual-mean NCEP wind and falls back to it). Both modes sample a regular lon/lat grid.

coastlines.label: Coastlines
coastlines.detail: Cells within ±200m of sea level rendered as a light grey-blue outline, stacked above all thematic layers to help locate land/sea boundaries in layers lacking terrain reference (NPP, domestication). On by default.

drag.description: Pan the map (2D) / rotate the globe (3D)

nKey.description: 3D globe view: reset to default camera (north pole up, equator facing you).

sunTime.description: Adjust subsolar longitude (diurnal, 0° = noon on the prime meridian), i.e. the day/night terminator position. Requires the lighting toggle on (off by default).

timeMode.description: Left-panel 'Time' control: switch between annual-average and monthly modes. Annual mode shows annual means (temperature/precipitation/wind) and sea-level pressure (subtropical highs); monthly mode picks a specific month via the season slider, and temperature/precipitation/pressure (seasonal anomaly ΔP)/wind follow it month-by-month.

timeSeason.description: The single slider in the 'Time' control has two roles: in monthly mode it snaps to 12 stops to pick a month (0 = March equinox, July = N. summer), and the solar declination follows so lighting stays consistent; in annual mode it sweeps 0–360° continuously, affecting only lighting (solar declination), not data. Tick labels switch between month names (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) and seasonal markers (equinox/solstice).

sunToggle.description: 2D/3D left panel: turn day/night lighting on/off (off by default). GPU-driven on both 2D and 3D. Settings synced via URL (?sun=&season=&night=) and shareable across 2D↔3D.

hoverCell.description: The right panel shows cell properties; selected cells take priority if any.

hoverLeave.description: Restores the planet summary when no cell is selected; the panel locks (no jump back) when a cell is selected.

ctrlClick.description: Append/remove from the selection (keeps existing). Standard desktop-app style.

dblClick.description: Select that cell (clearing others); deselect if it is already the only selection.

clickPlanet.description: In the 3D stellar view: opens the info panel and flies the camera to the body (the URL focus parameter is kept in sync, so refreshing or sharing the link returns to the same view). The panel groups orbit / physical / rotation & seasons / atmosphere / insolation fields; expand "🌍 Terrain data" if map data exists.

dblClickPlanet.description: In the 3D stellar view: the camera flies to and centers on the body immediately (zoom unchanged).

clean.description: Hides all UI and scene decoration (panels, status bar, graticule, polar axis), leaving only the map or globe — for video recording. Also reachable via the URL parameter ?clean=1. Exit with Esc or the hover-only top-right button.

spin.description: Slow continuous orbit of the 3D globe (~120s per revolution) for video recording. Pauses while dragging or during the N-key north-pole fly, resumes on release. Also reachable via ?spin=1; combined with clean view (?clean=1&spin=1) it is the standard recording posture.

dag.title: DAG Layer Architecture
dag.summary: World data is organized by discipline: physics → chemistry → astronomy → geological → climate → ecology → civilization. Upstream layer inputs drive downstream layer outputs, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) simulation pipeline.

branch.title: Branch System
branch.summary: Like a Git branch. Forks at a DAG layer, sharing all data above it and storing only the fork layer and below. Different branches of the same planet can have different land/sea distributions, climates, or civilizations.

cvt.title: CVT Spherical Mesh
cvt.summary: Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation — a uniform spherical mesh via Fibonacci spiral + Lloyd relaxation. All simulation (tectonics, climate, hydrology) runs directly on the spherical mesh, projected to a 2D raster only at final visualization.

cortial.title: Cortial 2019 Plate Tectonics
cortial.summary: Plate partition and evolution follow Cortial et al. (2019) Procedural Tectonic Planets: Poisson-disc seeds → spherical Voronoi partition → Euler-pole rotation → boundary re-detection → subduction/collision/erosion. See terrain-pipeline.md.

start.temperatureSamples: Try a climate experiment on the global map.
start.title: Getting started on the web

local.intro: Import your own heightmap, build a world, then choose a place to inspect or refine.

first.description: Choose a heightmap, check the elevation range, sea level, and preview, then save it to a world. If you do not have a heightmap, create a world from a template in the worlds list.

second.description: On the world page, confirm the branch and terrain grid size before selecting Build. When it finishes, open the map to see the available terrain and climate layers.

third.description: Use Region refinement on the flat map or globe. Choose Move to selection to centre the view, then View region. Inspect the original elevation or use the local options to refine terrain or extract rivers and lakes.

local.backup: To continue on another device, download a world backup from the World build panel. It includes regions saved in the world directory and can be restored with the command line.

static.intro: Explore published worlds or save your own regional elevation in this browser. To build a complete world, use the local app.

first.description: Choose a published world to open its map. To work with your own regional heightmap, create a browser world and import the source under World data.

second.action: Choose a region on the global map
second.description: Use Move to selection to centre the view, then choose View region. You can also open an imported heightmap directly from World data.

third.action: Learn how to refine and save terrain
third.description: When the region page offers browser refinement, generate a result and compare it with the source before saving or downloading it. The original elevation remains available without refinement.

static.backup: Before switching devices, export a browser data archive from World data and import it from the worlds list on the other device. The archive does not include published maps or cached models.

entries.title: Create a world
entries.content:
`dreamulator init <name> --template earthlike`

Create a new world from a template. Available templates: `minimal` (minimal config), `earthlike` (Earth-like planet).

entries.title: Run the simulation
entries.content:
`dreamulator build <world>`

Run all engines in DAG order: astronomy → geology (terrain+plates) → climate → ecology.

`dreamulator build <world> --only climate`

Run only the specified layer and any not-yet-run predecessors.

`dreamulator build <world> --force`

Force re-run all engines even if outputs already exist.

entries.title: Terrain generation
entries.content:
`dreamulator build <world> --only geological`

Run the geological layer and its prerequisites.

`dreamulator terrain info <world> -p <planet>`

View terrain statistics such as land and sea coverage and elevation.

entries.title: Start the server
entries.content:
`dreamulator serve --open`

Start the FastAPI server and open the browser. See README for Vite HMR dev mode.

`dreamulator serve --data-dir <path>`

Use a custom data directory.

entries.title: Branch management
entries.content:
`dreamulator branch create <world> <name> --at <layer>`

Fork a branch at a layer. E.g. `--at geological` → different land/sea under the same astronomy.

`dreamulator branch list <world>`

List all branches.

`dreamulator build <world> --branch <name>`

Run on a branch.

`dreamulator branch promote <world> <name> --as <new-world>`

Promote a branch to an independent world.

entries.title: Climate validation
entries.content:
`dreamulator climate validate <world>`

Validate climate accuracy against real Earth observations (Köppen group accuracy, precipitation RMSE, Cohen's Kappa). Requires ETOPO1 elevation data.

entries.title: AI narration
entries.content:
`dreamulator narrate <world>`

Generate a colloquial world description via the Claude API.

`dreamulator narrate <world> --branch <name>`

Narrate a specific branch.

`dreamulator narrate <world> -m <model>`

Specify an Anthropic model.

entries.title: Create a world
entries.content: Click "New World" on the "Worlds" page. Pick a template (`minimal` or `earthlike`), set a name and a random seed. The seed determines every procedural result — same seed + same input = an identical world.

entries.title: World structure
entries.content:
Each world organizes data by discipline:

```
physics → chemistry → astronomy → geological → climate → ecology → civilization
```

Each layer has `input/` (YAML, human-authored) and `derived/` (JSON, engine-computed). Engines read only from input and write only to derived — the LLM cannot "hallucinate" physics.

entries.title: Branch system
entries.content:
Branches are like Git branches. After forking at a DAG layer, they share all data above and store only the fork layer and below.

- Fork at `astronomy` → different star systems under the same physics
- Fork at `geological` → different land/sea under the same star system
- Fork at `climate` → different climate under the same geology

Branches switch via URL `?branch=<name>`, affecting all API queries and rendering.

entries.title: Build & validate
entries.content:
Select Build on the world page in the local app. After it finishes, open the map to view available terrain and climate. The world directory stores map products in `maps/<planet>/` and simulation results in `layers/<layer>/derived/`.

Check base settings checks the world configuration and YAML inputs for the base world. It does not run the simulation or verify the scientific accuracy of existing results.

entries.title: Time & monthly
entries.content: Use Annual and Monthly at the top of the inspector to change which data the map shows. When the selected layer has monthly data, the chart shows a mean for each month. Select a bar to display that month without running the model again. Layers without monthly data do not show a chart. On narrow screens, open Cells and statistics to find these controls.

entries.title: Day/night lighting
entries.content: The Lighting controls in the left panel set the time of day and the season. The time of day sets the subsolar longitude, and the season sets the subsolar latitude. Neither changes the selected data month. Lighting and month settings carry across the map and globe.

entries.title: Model grid and downscaling
entries.content: Under Main layers, Model grid shows the original grid results. Downscaled interpolates supported continuous fields such as temperature, precipitation, and pressure. When imported fine terrain and precipitation data are available, it also adjusts the temperature for elevation differences. This changes only the map display, not the simulation or overlays. The inspector and chart continue to use model-grid data.

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, and right-drag to pan. The scale and viewing distance appear below the scene.

Click a body or choose it from the Focus menu to select and center it without automatically zooming in. View orbit frames the primary body and the entire orbit, with a crosshair marking the selected body. View close-up frames the body itself. The selection is saved in the URL. Click empty space or choose No body selected to clear it.

entries.title: Planet textures
entries.content: Planets with map data auto-load terrain textures, showing real land/sea colors (not solid spheres). Textures are decoded from elevation PNGs into low-res equirectangular maps.

entries.title: Habitable zone
entries.content: A green ring marks the habitable zone (liquid water can exist on the surface), computed per Kopparapu et al. 2013 from stellar luminosity and effective temperature. The darker solid band is the conservative HZ (runaway greenhouse to maximum greenhouse); the fainter dashed halo is the optimistic HZ (recent Venus to early Mars). An eccentric orbit can briefly cross the conservative inner edge at perihelion — the orbit-averaged flux is the climatically relevant measure.

entries.title: Body details and maps
entries.content:
Click a body or its label in the scene to open its details. If you select a body from the dropdown, use Body details to open the panel. Go to flat map and Go to globe map appear in the toolbar only when the selected body has map data. Both links leave the stellar system view without needing to open the details first.

The details group orbital and physical properties, rotation and seasons, atmosphere and water, radiation and temperature, and plate tectonics. When terrain data is available, the panel also shows an elevation summary.

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
**Drag** — rotate
**Scroll** — zoom
**Right-drag / Ctrl+drag** — pan
**N key** — reset to default camera (north up, equator facing you)

**Ctrl+click** → append/remove a cell from the selection
**Double-click** → select a cell (clearing others); deselect if already the only one
**Esc** → clear all selections.

entries.title: Layer system
entries.content:
The left panel controls layer display, a four-slot compositing model:

1. **Base** — terrain shading (fixed)
2. **Thematic** — Köppen / Whittaker biomes / NPP / domestication (pick one)
3. **Fill** — plate shading (stacks over thematic)
4. **Feature** — boundaries, coastlines, current arrows (always on top)

Each layer has independent opacity. With no overlays the base is sampled directly at zero extra cost.

entries.title: Cell inspector
entries.content:
The right panel switches by selection:

**0 selected** — shows the hovered cell (coords, elevation, crust, plate, climate); leaving → planet summary
**1 selected** — locks that cell (no jump back on mouse leave)
**>1 selected** — multi-select stats (count, area, elevation range/mean, mean temp/precip, dominant Köppen)

Selected cells highlight yellow; hovered cells highlight blue.

The single-cell「📊 Climate descriptors」group shows the continuous UCC descriptors (time-weighted mean temperature, seasonal range, time below 0°C, reference-year precipitation, aridity index AI, same-period deficit, precipitation concentration), independent of monthly mode; maps without a climate build (including the Earth reference root) show a fallback hint instead.

entries.title: Overview
entries.content:
The civilization map draws fictional territories on real Earth administrative boundaries. Province boundaries (ADM1) support individual edits. National boundaries (ADM0) support painting an entire country at once. The optional external basemap is off by default in the full-screen view.

If local boundaries are missing, run `uv run python scripts/dev/prepare_civmap_data.py` from the project root, then reload the map. The static site can only show published boundaries and territories.

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
In a world's **Civilization** tab, select **Open civilization map** above the documents. The map opens for the current branch.

Editing is locked by default in the local app. Select **Editing locked** to unlock it, then choose a country and click the map to paint. Select **Editing enabled** to lock it again. Use **Undo** or Ctrl+Z (⌘Z on macOS) to undo the last territory edit. The static site is read-only.

entries.title: Set the centre and size
entries.content:
Open **Region refinement** on the global map or globe. Enter the centre latitude and longitude in degrees. Positive latitude is north, and positive longitude is east. The side length is the physical size of a square region, not the resolution: 550 km means a 550 × 550 km region.

While the panel is open, a click on the map (a tap on touch screens) fills that point as the centre; dragging the map does not pick. You can also select one map cell and choose **Use selected point** (on desktop, hold Ctrl or Command and click; on a touchscreen, tap the map). That fills in the cell centre and leaves the side length unchanged.

entries.title: Move to the selection
entries.content:
Choose **Move to selection** to centre the map or globe on the selected region. A white dashed outline with a dark border marks the area. If you drag the view away, choose the button again to return to the centre without changing the coordinates.

The centre and side length are also stored in the URL. Reloading, reopening the URL or switching views centres the view on the same region. **Clear selection** removes the outline and the selection from the URL without deleting any maps. Moving the view does not build, refine or export a map.

entries.title: View the selected region
entries.content: Choose **Move to selection**, then **View region**. Both the local and static sites open a preview from the global heightmap, even without an existing regional map. **Back to the global selection** returns to the original map or globe and centres it on the selection. Set the output size and download the result on the regional map page.

entries.title: Open a regional map
entries.content: Open **View region** from a global selection to see the original terrain cropped from the global heightmap. The current world and branch stay visible at the top even when the sidebar is collapsed. On the local site, use **Regional data source** to open saved results for the same region. Switching does not rerun refinement or change the global map. You can also open saved regions from the world's **World data** page.

entries.title: Browse and change the display
entries.content: A dashed line marks the region. The surroundings show available world terrain for reference, and the graticule crosses the boundary. Choose **Frame region and surroundings** to recenter, or use **Fit region** and **Fill view** without world context. Use **Map elevation** to compare the original and refined terrain. **Regional source** and **TD input grid** switch all TD conditions together without affecting map elevation or hydrology. Grid resampling is not downscaling. Hover to inspect a point, double-click to lock it, or tap on a touchscreen. The inspector expands the section for the active layer. Select **Refine terrain** in the bottom left to see the device and settings. Read-only results show **Elevation & export** instead.

entries.title: Inspect a location
entries.content: Hover inside the region to read the selected raster. The regional source records annual mean surface temperature; the TD grid uses temperature adjusted to sea level. Historical results are not filled with current world data. Browser refinement uses only elevation. River accumulation measures relative upstream contributions, not discharge in cubic metres per second.

entries.title: Download elevation
entries.content: Open **Refine terrain** or **Elevation & export** in the bottom left, then choose the elevation source, size, and format. The default 16-bit grayscale PNG maps the region’s elevation range from black to white. Choose 32-bit floating-point TIFF if you need pixel values in metres. Both formats record the source and bounds in their image description. A larger output simply interpolates the source; it does not refine the terrain. Global extracts can be downloaded on either site. Downloads from existing regional maps default to their native size.

entries.title: Generate and compare terrain locally
entries.content:
On the local site, open a selection with monthly climate or a square regional map with refinement inputs. Open **Generate refined terrain**. **Redraw** and **Blend in details** use Terrain Diffusion: one draws new landforms and the other adds small features to the original. Both compute rivers and lakes afterwards. Choose **Hydrology only** to compute rivers and lakes from the original elevation without loading the model.

In **Advanced settings**, the channel threshold sets how much upstream accumulation is needed to draw a river. A lower value shows more tributaries. Leave it blank for the grid-based default. Confirm the window and grid size before starting. The result is saved as a separate regional map. You can refresh to check the running job.

entries.title: Refine terrain in the browser
entries.content:
Open **Generate refined terrain (browser experiment)** to see the compute budget. **Source row spacing** is the ground distance between adjacent rows of pixels in the current image. **Output spacing** is the distance between adjacent pixels in the generated image.

**Native spacing** is the ground distance between neighbouring elevation cells before the data was enlarged. If the original data has one elevation value every 360 metres, enter 0.36 km. If it has one every 50 kilometres, enter 50 even if the image was enlarged later. Only blending requires this value.

**Redraw** generates terrain from the broad shapes in the source. **Redraw with stronger details** lets you adjust the amplitude of fine detail, which defaults to twice that of the standard redraw. Both methods can change valleys and coastlines. **Blend in details** keeps the source coastline and seabed and adds small features on land. Leave the blend scale blank to use four times the native spacing. With a native spacing of 0.36 km, details start blending in below about 1.44 km.

Change the random seed under **Advanced settings** to generate a different terrain with the same settings. To download the input, open **Original elevation map** below. Choose a small selection for your first run. The three methods share the same 1.14 GB model files. Later runs can reuse the browser cache.

- `docs/design/vision.md` — long-term vision & philosophy

entries.title: Overview
entries.content:
The sky view shows what is visible from a point on a celestial body at a given time. The top readout keeps the observer, location, instant in Earth days since epoch, and selected target in view. Observation and Display are below it, and the time controls are at the bottom. These controls fade when idle. Move over the chart, press Tab, or choose Show controls to bring them back. Hide controls keeps them out of the way until you choose to show them again.

In Look mode, drag to look around, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Click a body to open its details. In Display settings, switch to All-sky to see the whole hemisphere, or turn on coordinate grids, the rise/set almanac, and the below-horizon list. The URL records the observer, location, instant, direction, grids, panels, and world branch so you can share the view.

entries.title: Chart conventions
entries.content: The Look mode is natural perspective: facing north, east is on your right and the zenith is up; the horizon is a curve with the ground below it, azimuth ticks and eight cardinal labels along it. The All-sky disc is the looking-up projection: N top, E left (the planisphere convention, mirrored relative to a looking-down map). Both views share one marker language: disc size encodes angular diameter, stars carry their black-body colour, the crescent shows phase (lit limb toward the star), dimmed markers are below the naked-eye limit (mag ≥ 6). Display settings can overlay the horizon grid (alt/az), the equatorial grid (RA/dec with the celestial equator highlighted) and the ecliptic line. The clock is an epoch-relative day count plus a solar-day fraction, not local midnight time.

entries.title: Time controls
entries.content: Enter a day count and press Enter to set the observation time. The unit button switches between the observer's solar days and Earth days. The slider sets playback speed, not the date. When playback pauses, the almanac and event predictions update for that instant.

entries.title: Rise/set and events
entries.content: Below the chart, bodies under the horizon list with their next rise; the right inspector shows the selected body's phase, illuminance, elongations and equatorial/ecliptic coordinates. Inside the polar circles a body may cross the horizon only once per season — the missing event shows as empty (deferred to the engine's M4 event search).

entries.title: Sky cultures (asterism lines)
entries.content: The Display dialog's asterism-lines toggle (URL parameter cul) draws the civilization layer's sky cultures: cultures name background stars and connect them into figures strictly by id (authored in sky_culture.yaml; every reference is validated at build time). In the look-around view, hovering a figure brightens it and shows the culture's asterism name, and clicking opens the inspector (culture, member stars with magnitudes, meaning). An authored star's inspector also lists each culture's proper name for it. The toggle stays hidden for worlds without sky cultures.
